resources.string: Files live in Android/data/<package>/files/logs. The oldest sessions are pruned automatically.
Bundles the recent sessions and sends them to the relay, which notifies you by Bark.
Writes each session to a file on the head unit. Retained: %1$d files, %2$s. Also shows debug lines on screen.
Automatic (USB if plugged in, otherwise wireless)
Accepts the system USB permission dialog for a plugged-in iPhone automatically. Needs accessibility access.
Accepts the system dialog that asks whether to allow the CarPlay app to access a plugged-in iPhone over USB, so wired CarPlay can start without a tap on the head unit screen.
Enable this app under Settings > Accessibility to auto-confirm the USB prompt.
iPhone detected on USB; switching to wired CarPlay
Uses the MFi credential bundled with the app. No coprocessor or document selection is required.
The bundled MFi credential is missing from this build.
Address must start with http:// or https://. Token is optional and sent as an Authorization bearer token.
Select a DER PKCS#7 certificate and its matching unencrypted DER PKCS#8 private key. Documents are reloaded when MFI reconnects.

Join the head unit and iPhone to the same Wi-Fi network (for example a home router or a phone hotspot). No hotspot is created; the head unit keeps using its current Wi-Fi.
The head unit is not connected to any Wi-Fi
If the head unit is on 2.4 GHz after connecting, it scans and switches to the same Wi-Fi network\'s 5 GHz band automatically (needs the head unit ADB channel).

When the head unit is on 2.4 GHz, scan and reassociate to the same Wi-Fi network\'s 5 GHz band to restore 5 GHz speed. Needs the head unit ADB channel; if it cannot switch, the status honestly stays 2.4 GHz.
Ask Android for a 5 GHz LocalOnlyHotspot; a 2.4 GHz client is dropped first. Android 13+ only.

Preselect the 5 GHz hotspot channel, default 36 (36-48 has the widest compatibility; some head units cannot use 149-165 under their regulatory domain). The channel is read back from the radio after the write, so a lock that did not stick shows the real channel.
Set the system hotspot to the 5 GHz band and raise it via tethering. Uses the head unit\'s own ADB channel (no root/Magisk needed); drops Wi-Fi while it starts.
Channel: asked for %1$d, radio is on %2$d.

No local ADB channel is available on this device.
On launch, raise the head unit\'s own wireless ADB (loopback adbd) so the 5 GHz hotspot can reach a root shell without root/Magisk. Needs the vendor wifiadb support; harmless where it is absent.
Wireless ADB is ready as root (port %1$d).
Wireless ADB is not available on this device.
Report Android location to the iPhone
Sends precise Android location as CarPlay GPS data when the iPhone requests it.
Start CarPlay automatically after device boot
Brings CarPlay back to the screen when the head unit wakes from sleep after the car is switched on, without reading screen content.
Sleep-wake keepalive off — enable this app under Settings > Accessibility
This unit usually sleeps instead of powering off, and a wake from sleep sends no boot signal. Keepalive relies on this app\'s accessibility service to bring CarPlay back after the car is switched on.
Route AAOS audio buses by CarPlay audio type
Which bus navigation prompts play on. Auto routes them by CarPlay audio type; pick a channel if the head unit sends them to the wrong place.
Which bus music plays on. Auto routes it by CarPlay audio type; pick a channel to force it elsewhere.
Play CarPlay media over the head unit\'s Bluetooth (A2DP) instead of Wi-Fi. Calls, navigation and Siri stay on Wi-Fi. Off by default.
Bluetooth audio enabled, but A2DP is not connected yet. Connect the phone over Bluetooth, or switch the channel back to CarPlay to hear media.
Lower resolution needs less USB bandwidth and is more stable on wired CarPlay
Scales the whole picture live as you drag, and adjusts CarPlay icon/text density after reconnect.

iOS 26/27 video in car. While on, the car always reports P gear so the iPhone hands over its video, which plays in an overlay over CarPlay (both stay visible and touchable). Video needs a plain http(s) source; FairPlay (Apple TV+) items cannot play.

Which audio path CarLife uses. CarLife: standard usage (USAGE_ASSISTANT for navigation), works on any head unit - this is what the bundled CarLife engine used. Wuling: also writes the head unit\'s cp_media/cp_navi tags so navigation ducks music on the factory channel. Takes effect on reconnect.
Resolution requested from the phone. 1080p is sharper; 720p raises the frame rate on congested 2.4 GHz links. Applies after the next CarLife reconnect.

Hplay is free to use: no paid edition, no activation code, no subscription or in-app purchase. It is published as open source under GPL-3.0; any channel charging you on its behalf is unrelated to the developer.

This software is developed independently. It is not affiliated with, authorised by, or partnered with SAIC-GM-Wuling or its affiliates, nor with the developers of 「哨了个兵」 or 菱粉桌面. Product names appear only to describe the devices and software environments this app is compatible with.

On supported head units this app can use the public interfaces exposed by desktops such as Wuling 「哨了个兵」 and 菱粉桌面 to read vehicle state (battery, gear, doors, climate) and to issue a limited set of controls. Availability depends on the desktop version and the car model; when an interface is missing the related features are hidden instead of showing made-up data.

Vehicle, media and location data are processed on this device only and are not uploaded unless you initiate it. When talking to a third-party desktop or plugin, how that party handles the data is up to them; check their privacy policy yourself.
Use this software only when it is safe to do so and do not operate the screen while driving. The result of any vehicle control is whatever the car actually does.
